title: Long-context cache behavior mapping and version-lock automation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Produce a reproducible per-model mapping of cache behavior across realistic sequence-length distributions, and build an automated version-lock (version-locking) policy that recommends when a model should be served from a stable binary/quantization candidate to avoid tail-latency regressions. This ticket covers the measurement harness, profile schema, ingest pipeline for model+sequence signatures, and a first-pass automation that suggests locking candidates for the release engineering and model-ops teams.

Background: We routinely see that models with similar nominal architectures exhibit different KV cache retention and eviction characteristics under heavy long-context tails. Currently, engineers onboard models with ad-hoc heuristics and manual checks. That process is slow and error-prone for large model catalogs. The intent here is to formalize measurement, export a compact per-model profile, and surface automated recommendations for version-locking when a model's runtime variant (e.g., q4_0 vs q8_0, or fused-kernel build) shows measurable tail-latency or throughput regressions beyond an SLA threshold.

Scope and deliverables:
- Measurement harness that replays representative request distributions (short/median/long tails) against candidate runtime variants; captures latencies, KV cache hit/evict stats, per-step token CPU/GPU times, and memory high-water marks.
- Profile schema (JSON lines) with: model_id, model_version, runtime_variant_tag, seq_length_quantiles, kv_hit_rate_by_bucket, tail_latency_p99/p995, steady_throughput_tokens_per_sec, observed_memory_peak_bytes, dataset_signature, and provenance metadata.
- Ingest pipeline: periodic runs produce profile artifacts to an S3 prefix and register metadata in the model catalog (internal ML portal).
- Recommendation engine (initial): a rule-based automation that compares latest production variant vs candidate variant across defined SLO deltas and emits a recommendation object: keep-as-default | recommend-lock | require-investigation. These appear as suggestions in the onboarding checklist UI and as a note in the model's catalog entry.
- Migration/runbook for rollout: how to interpret recommendations, manual override, and fallback steps if a lock causes customer throughput regressions.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Measurement runs execute reproducibly in CI for 90% of community-onboarded models and produce profile artifacts that validate against the schema.
2) Profiles show per-quantile seq-length distributions (0.5/0.9/0.99) and kv-hit metrics; p99 latencies are computed and compared between variants.
3) Recommendation engine flags regression for any candidate variant with >10% p99 increase or >15% throughput decrease while memory usage increases by >5% (configurable thresholds).
4) Model catalog receives profile metadata and displays the recommendation status.
5) Documentation (Confluence) and a short runbook are published and linked in the ticket.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We will start with rule-based thresholds to avoid early false positives from noisy samples; this will be replaced by a lightweight statistical test in a follow-up ticket if warranted.
- To reduce infra cost, initial measurement runs will sample 5k request traces per model across synthetic and replayed traffic rather than full production capture.
- Profile artifacts must be compact (<= 256KB per profile) so they can be retained across many versions. The schema will store quantiles and aggregated counters rather than raw traces.
- We prefer running the harness in Dedicated staging pools to match infra topology of production and avoid resource skew. If not possible, we'll annotate the profile provenance as 'staging-simulated'.

Telemetry and dashboards:
- Add Grafana panels for: distribution of observed p99 deltas across onboarding runs; fraction of models recommended for locking; top models by memory pressure increase.
- Emit structured events to the observability pipeline: onboarding.profile.generated, onboarding.recommendation.emitted, onboarding.lock.applied. Each event includes model_id and variant_tag.

Rollout plan:
1) Prototype harness and schema (this ticket) -> internal team review.
2) Run on 25 pilot models (mix of small/medium/large families) -> collect feedback.
3) Wire recommendations into onboarding UI (read-only for first release).
4) After two weeks and zero critical false positives, enable suggestions in the checklist with manual accept.
5) Iterate on thresholds and add statistical test in follow-up.

Risks and mitigations:
- False positives: start read-only and require human accept before automated locking.
- Cost: cap sampling runs and reuse cached prefixes; store only aggregates.
- Metric drift: include dataset_signature + harness-version to detect incompatible profile comparisons.

comments: 2025-11-04 - Aisha Patel: Initial spike completed. Harness can run replayed traces at 2x real-time on staging dedicated nodes. Observed that some large LLM families show multi-modal seq-length behavior that requires per-bucket kv stats.
2025-11-06 - Marco Ruiz (review): Suggest adding dataset_signature field to avoid comparing profiles across different prompt distributions. Also ask to include harness-version in metadata.

2025-11-09 - Dev (Devon Park): Began implementation of ingest lambda. Found an edge-case where quantile computation diverges for tiny sample counts; added deterministic minimum sample requirement and fallback to synthetic extrapolation.

2025-11-11 - Lei Chen (SRE): Noted that running the full pilot on dedicated staging will need quota bump for GPU pool during 11/16-11/20; requesting approval from infra. Filing INF-227 to track quota change.

2025-11-15 - Evan Brooks (PM): Reviewed acceptance criteria and asked to tighten the p99 threshold for 'recommend-lock' to 8% for high-value customers. We'll make the threshold configurable and annotate which recommendation used which threshold.
2025-11-17 - Devon Park: Profile schema v1 published to S3 and registered in model catalog. Running initial 25-model pilot tomorrow. Next: dashboard panels and recommendation UI hook.
